newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower, pension funds on sidelines.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower, pension funds on sidelines.

text.p: Shares ended Monday lower on frozen sentiment, with many investors sitting out the session ahead of the year's close, brokers said.
Buying by pension funds, which had been expected to boost the market, was limited, they added.
The composite stock index ended down 8.33 points to provisionally close at 684.81.
"Local clients are sidelined and foreigners have closed their books for the year," said Casey Choe of UBS Securities. "No one is really interested in buying now."

News that Dongshin Construction had applied for court receivership after defaulting on debt payments had a minor impact on overall sentiment, brokers said. The shares last traded at 3,870 won per share, after being halted on Saturday.
Declining shares beat advancers 644 to 236. Volume was thin, as 21.5 million shares changed hands.
Brokers said it was difficult to estimate how much pension funds have been buying, but it appeared to be less than the 30 billion won per day that had been hoped for.
Blue chips were mixed. Samsung Electronics fell 1,600 won to 46,000, while Korea Mobile Telecom rose 19,000 to 465,000.

Sammi Steel remained on top of the most active stocks list on Monday after profit-taking hit the shares. They fell 330 won to 4,380. Sammi had risen on news that it planned to sell parts of its stainless steel business to POSCO.
Samsung Engineering and six other initial public offerings will begin trading on Tuesday. Hyundai Electronics will be listed on Thursday.
